questions.prompt: Put the phases in order, starting from new moon.
What causes the phases of the Moon?
options: Earth’s shadow covering part of the Moon
How much of the Moon’s sunlit half we can see from Earth as it orbits
questions.explain: The Sun always lights half the Moon; our view of that half changes.

questions.prompt: About how many days are there from one Purnima (full moon) to the next?
questions.explain: The lunar month is about 29.5 days.

options: the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon
the Moon is at first quarter
the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth
the Sun is between the Earth and the Moon
questions.explain: The Moon’s shadow falls on Earth, at new moon.

questions.prompt: On which night can a lunar eclipse happen?
questions.explain: Only at full moon is the Moon on the far side of Earth, where Earth’s shadow falls.

questions.prompt: Why don’t we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The Moon’s orbit is tilted about 5°, so its shadow usually misses Earth
questions.explain: The Moon must be near a node, where its orbit crosses Earth’s orbital plane.

questions.prompt: In the Moon Lab, the Moon rose at about 6 pm. What phase was it?
questions.explain: The full Moon is opposite the Sun, so it rises as the Sun sets.

questions.text: When the lit part of the Moon grows, it is ___. When it shrinks, it is ___.
questions.explain: Shukla paksha is waxing; Krishna paksha is waning.
